slides.say: For every two numbers x and y, two operations are defined. Diamond of x, y is x squared minus two x y plus y squared, and hash of x, y is x squared plus two x y plus y squared. Hash of diamond of ten, six, and diamond of five, four, is equal to what?
Two operations in one question, the diamond and the hash. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, the standard way, and then with the shortcut formulas.

[short pause] Inside the hash there are two diamonds. So we calculate both diamonds first, and then the hash works on the two results. That's three calculations. The left diamond is diamond of ten and six, so x is ten and y is six. Ten squared is a hundred. Two times ten times six is a hundred twenty, and it's subtracted. Six squared is thirty-six. A hundred minus a hundred twenty is negative twenty, plus thirty-six is sixteen.

The right diamond is diamond of five and four. Five squared is twenty-five. Two times five times four is forty, subtracted. Four squared is sixteen. Twenty-five minus forty is negative fifteen, plus sixteen is one.

Now the hash of sixteen and one. Sixteen squared is two hundred fifty-six. Two times sixteen times one is thirty-two. One squared is one. Two hundred fifty-six plus thirty-two is two hundred eighty-eight, plus one is two hundred eighty-nine. Choice number two is our answer.
at: Choice number two is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Another way is to recognize the shortcut formulas inside the definitions. x squared minus two x y plus y squared is the formula for x minus y, all squared. And x squared plus two x y plus y squared is x plus y, all squared.
at: x y plus y squared is x

slides.say: So diamond of ten and six is ten minus six, which is four, squared, sixteen. Diamond of five and four is five minus four, which is one, squared, one.

And the hash of sixteen and one is sixteen plus one, which is seventeen, squared. Seventeen squared is seventeen times seventeen. Seventeen times ten is a hundred seventy, and seventeen times seven is a hundred nineteen. Together, two hundred eighty-nine. Choice number two. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
